headline: MSCI confirmed it will drop Strategy, the biggest bitcoin-holding company, from its MSCI USA index at the end of November; bitcoin sits near $74,000 while traders price in a December Fed rate hike.

stories.title: MSCI will drop Strategy from its main indexes on 30 November
stories.summary: In its November review, released after the US close on Wednesday, MSCI confirmed it will remove Strategy (MSTR) from the MSCI USA index under its new rule for 'non-operating companies'. Funds that copy MSCI indexes will have to sell their Strategy shares by the end of the month.
points: Metaplanet, Yellow Cake and Upexi were also removed, per Bitcoin Magazine; SharpLink was not removed, per The Block.
The changes take effect at the close on 30 Nov, per Bitcoin Magazine.
Strategy shares closed at $122.35 and were down 1.51% at $120.50 after hours as of 5:34pm ET, per Bitcoin Magazine; The Block reported a 2.6% after-hours drop to $119.06.
JPMorgan estimated about $2.8B of index-fund selling, up to $8.8B if other index providers follow; the estimate was made for an earlier version of MSCI's proposal, per Bitcoin Magazine.
Strategy holds 850,364 BTC bought at an average of $75,456, per Bitcoin Magazine.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $74,000 as a December rate hike looks almost certain
stories.summary: Bitcoin sat out a strong rebound in tech stocks on Wednesday after Tuesday's hotter-than-expected US inflation report. Futures markets now price a Fed rate hike at the 8-9 December meeting as near certain. Higher rates make savings and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money away from risky assets like crypto.
points: October consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month, hotter than expected, per CoinDesk.
CME FedWatch on 10 Nov showed 88.8% odds of a quarter-point December hike and 11.2% for a half-point hike, per Investing.com.
Bitcoin's low on Tuesday was $72,700, and about $725M of crypto futures bets were forcibly closed in 24 hours, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin was at about $74,622 early Wednesday evening (US time), per The Motley Fool.

stories.title: Money keeps leaving bitcoin funds
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin funds had a fourth straight day of net outflows on Tuesday. If the trend holds to December, 2026 would be the first calendar year since these funds launched with more money pulled out than put in, per Bitcoin.com.
points: Tuesday 10 Nov: $95.0M left US spot bitcoin ETFs, with BlackRock's IBIT down $78.2M, per TFTC's ETF tracker.
Earlier daily outflows: $430.2M on 5 Nov, $411.9M on 6 Nov and $201.0M on 9 Nov, per CryptoDataAPI.
The funds are about $1.1B in net outflows for 2026, with $92.82B in total assets, per Bitcoin.com.
Tether's USDT supply fell $6.6B over 60 days, per CryptoQuant data cited by CoinDesk.

briefs.title: SEC sides with the CFTC on stock 'perpetual futures'
briefs.summary: The SEC filed a brief backing the CFTC against a lawsuit that seeks to undo its approval of never-expiring futures on single stocks, which Coinbase, Kalshi and Kraken's parent applied to list, per The Block.

briefs.title: Big banks added bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter
briefs.summary: Barclays raised its IBIT stake 48% to about $187M and Citigroup opened a roughly $119M position in Fidelity's bitcoin ETF, per The Motley Fool; these are 30 Sep holdings.

briefs.title: London eases rules for crypto exchange-traded notes
briefs.summary: The London Stock Exchange relaxed admission rules for crypto ETNs sold to professional investors, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Gram jumps after Telegram founder's comments
briefs.summary: Gram rose about 13.6% to $1.24 after Telegram's founder called it undervalued, per CoinDesk.
